children: Alimentation Couche-Tard recorded higher profit and revenue in the first quarter, driven by growth in road transportation fuel sales.
The Canadian convenience-store operator on Tuesday posted a first-quarter profit of $828.5 million, or 90 cents a share, compared with $782.5 million, or 82 cents a share, a year earlier.
Adjusted earnings per share were 90 cents, compared with analyst estimates of 89 cents, according to FactSet.
Revenue gained 25% to $21.7 billion, compared with analyst estimates of $20.86 billion.
Road transportation fuel revenue climbed 33% to $16.67 billion. The increase was mainly due to higher average fuel selling price, partly offset by softer demand, the company said.
Merchandise and service revenue rose 4.1% to $4.88 billion, primarily due to a boost from acquisitions.

The results come after the Circle K owner said in July it plans to acquire Poland's largest convenience retailer Zabka for about $8.7 billion. The deal would mark Couche-Tard's largest-ever acquisition after it abandoned a $47 billion takeover attempt of Seven & i, the Japanese owner of 7-Eleven, last year.
